utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Come in, Derek. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I'm furious. My business partner stole money from me. I want to make him pay. I'm going to hurt him if I see him.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: I have to take what you're saying very seriously, Derek. When you say you're going to hurt him — I need you to be clear with me. Are you describing a physical threat against him? Because if you're telling me you intend to harm a specific person, I have a legal and ethical obligation to take steps to protect them. That may include contacting him or law enforcement. I want to make sure I understand exactly what you mean.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I mean... I just want to confront him. I'm not going to actually do anything. I'm just so angry.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: I'm relieved to hear that. Your anger is completely understandable. I need to document what you said and I'm obligated to warn the person if there's a credible threat, so I want you to be honest with me throughout our sessions. Can we talk about what confronting him would actually look like in a safe and legal way?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Yeah. I don't want to do anything stupid. I just want justice.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Let's focus on that. I want to help you pursue this through the right channels — a lawyer, the police if money was stolen. Your anger is valid and we can use it constructively.
